newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to allow foreign primary dealers in OLOs.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to allow foreign primary dealers in OLOs.

text.p: The Belgian Treasury has agreed with the 15 primary dealers in Belgian state debt that in the future foreign-based banks can be allowed to become primary dealers in Belgian linear bonds and Treasury bills, market sources told Reuters on Thursday.

Treasury director Gregoir Brouhns declined to give details, but said that the Treasury had held talks about adapting the primary dealers regulation book to the European Union Investment Services Directive (ISD).
The Treasury is due to make a statement about this on Thursday afternoon.
The ISD, which came into force in January 1996, allows banks and brokerages authorised on their domestic markets to offer financial services in other EU states.
Current Belgian primary dealer regulations state that primary dealers have to be based in Belgium or Luxembourg.
But in January, the Brussels branch of Deutsche Bank AG, one of the 15 primary dealers of Belgian state debt, moved most of its linear bond (OLO) trading activity from Brussels to London.
The move has sparked calls to adjust the rule-book and to allow other foreign-based banks to operate as primary dealers.

Dealers said that the Belgian Treasury had received several requests from foreign banks to become primary dealers in Belgian debt in the run up to a single currency in 1999, provided they were allowed to operate from London.

The primary dealer system, set up in 1991, requires selected dealers to make a market in OLOs by continuously quoting bid and ask prices. They are allowed to take part in the Treasury's non-competitive OLO and Treasury bill auctions and enjoy a preferential relationship with the central bank.
